description.purpose: The container this person's applications are instantiated into. It ships empty and open: no cells, no ports, no contract of its own. An APP is a specific composition and specific code that came out of a build order -- a derived template in the library, tagged `app` -- and what it produces is a VIEW. It is not a channel: a channel is how the person is reached, an app is something the person's screen shows. It stands beside `./channels` and `./assistants` rather than inside either, because an app belongs to the PERSON: it outlives a generation swap the way a channel does, and two of the person's agents may hold views on the same screen it writes to.
description.use_when: Never on its own -- it travels with the member level. One app is one node instantiated into this container at the name it is known by (`colony-view`, a project board, a day plan), and an app is instantiated, never shipped. AN APP HAS NO PORT AND NO SURFACE OF ITS OWN: it writes views onto a display, and the display is a channel of this same member. Whatever authentication stands in front of that screen stands in front of the app; giving an app a port would be a second front door nobody counted. TRANSIT, two lanes in each direction -- OUT, from an app up into the level: `view` (one picture towards a screen, carried on by the level's own `./apps -> ./channels` edge, which is guarded on a non-empty `context.channel`, so the app's OWN outbound edge is where the screen is named -- a literal in one edge, because an app is deliberately display-blind) and `error`. IN, from the level down into an app: `event` (somebody acted on a view this app owns) and `receipt` (a write this app made was refused). Both keep their lane name on the way down, because which inbound lane an app has is the app's business and the per-app edge is what names it. The level ships the level-side half of all four; what an instantiating mutation adds is the node and the edges that bind it to this container by name.
description.not_in_scope: No ports, for the same load-bearing reason ./assistants and ./channels declare none: a sealed hive refuses exactly the endpoints an app instantiation needs (hive_port_boundary), and the pairing edge between this container and an app below it is such an endpoint. No slot: GH #285's slot governs an address that does not exist, and this container does exist, so the declared unbound word could never fire -- see unbound_slot_behaviour in crates/meclaw-colony/src/colony.rs, which steps aside as soon as the target is a registered hive scope. No params.contract either: this container is wired by its own level the moment the member is instantiated, so mutation::hive_contract::check_lane_doors sees a WIRED hive from birth (hive_path_is_wired) and would then owe a door inside for every declared accepts lane -- and a member with no app yet is a legitimate state, and the ordinary one. No cells. And no view of its own: the smallest view there is is a prose block, and every agent has that without an app at all (GH #455) -- an app is what you build when the picture is worth code, not what you need before a person can be shown a paragraph.
